{{Short description|British actuary (1899–1981)}}

[[File:Gladys Gregory FamiltyPhoto1.jpg|thumb|Gladys Gregory (1899–1981)]]
'''Gladys Caroline Gregory''' (19 May 1899{{snd}} 6 November 1981) was one of two women to share the accolade of first woman [[actuary]] in the United Kingdom, the other being [[Dorothy Spiers]], née Davis. Gregory joined [[Prudential Assurance]] in 1917, direct from school, and passed the actuarial exams at the [[Institute of Actuaries]] in 1923.

==Early life and education==

Gladys Caroline Gregory was born on 19 May 1899 at 32 Mina Road, [[Walworth]], London and was the eldest daughter of [[shoemaker]], Thomas Gregory (1871–1966), and his wife, Harriet Elizabeth Gregory, née Cobbett (1870–1958).<ref>Births (CR) England & Wales. St Saviour, Southwark, London. Q2 1899. GREGORY, Gladys Caroline. Vol: 1D; p. 147.</ref>  She attended the local council school in [[Clapham]] where she gained the school-leaving certificate.<ref>''South Western Star''. (1917). Broomwood Secondary School: War Work of Learned Women. 23 March; p5f&ndash;g.</ref>

==Career==

Gregory joined Prudential Assurance in July 1917 when she was 18.<ref>Prudential Archives. Employee Records.</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Bowsher |first=Liz |date=2023-09-07 |title='City Surprised': the first women Fellows |url=https://www.theactuary.com/2023/09/07/city-surprised-first-women-fellows |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=The Actuary |language=en}}</ref> In November 1919 ''The Institute of Actuaries'' voted to admit women on the same conditions as men.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41136946|title=Admission of women to membership. Special General Meeting, 24 November 1919|journal =Journal of the Institute of Actuaries|volume=52|pages=111&ndash;114|year=1920|last1=Thorne|first1=A. C. |last2=Elderton|first2= W. Palin|last3= Trouncer|first3=H. M. |jstor=41136946 }}</ref> Gregory passed her first exam in 1920 and the subsequent exams in each year afterwards, qualifying in 1923, alongside Dorothy Davis.<ref>Institute and Faculty of Actuaries. (1923) Membership Cards: GREGORY, Gladys.</ref> Passing the exams was clearly a shared endeavour - Dorothy and Gladys “''coached''” and did their “''very hard swotting''” together, for “…''the ‘stiffest’ tests in mathematics''”, qualifying in less than the “''usual four years''”.<ref name="mirror">{{Cite news |date=1923-06-19 |title=First Women As Acturies |pages=2 |work=Daily Mirror |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/daily-mirror-first-women-as-acturies/136150659/ |access-date=2023-12-02}}</ref><ref>''Portsmouth Evening News'', (1923) Women’s Siege of The Professions.  p. 7g.</ref> In 1923 Gregory was the more prominent of the pair: at 24 she was two years younger than her counterpart; her final examination was said to have been “''faultless''”, and she would have come overall first had the results been ranked.<ref name=mirror/> Writing in ''Good Housekeeping'' in October 1923, she commended the profession to well-educated girls, prepared to work hard and give up their evenings to study. She also made the point that many insurance offices were overstaffed, and opportunities for girls were limited.<ref>Gregory, Gladys. (1923) ‘Actuarial Work As A Career For Women’. In: ''Good Housekeeping''. October; pp. 49, 162-164</ref>
==Personal and later life==

Gladys resigned from Prudential in April 1927, shortly before she married John Brooker, and she formally resigned as a Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries in October 1927.<ref>Marriages (CR) England & Wales. Wandsworth, London. Q2 1927. GREGORY, Gladys C and BROOKER, John. Vol: 1D; p. 1284.</ref><ref name=":0" /> After their marriage, she became a housewife and had two daughters.<ref>1939 Register, England & Wales. 39 Station Road, Wokingham, Berkshire. BROOKER, Gladys, C. Ref: RG101/2061D/012/30 Letter Code: DTLA. </ref> Gregory died on 16 November 1981 in [[Wokingham]], [[Berkshire]].<ref>Deaths Index (CR) England & Wales. Reading & Wokingham, Berkshire. Q4 1981. BROOKER, Gladys Caroline. Vol: 19; p. 0501.</ref><ref>Testamentary Records England. 4 March 1982. BROOKER, Gladys Caroline. Probate Calendar.  England & Wales Government Probate Death Index 1858-2019.</ref>
